# #146 — Roll out shared-kb wording to clients, skills, and runtime docs

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none

## Goal

Update all Open Brain client-facing docs, skills, generated help, and runtime guidance so users and agents only speak `shared-kb` for shared Open Brain knowledge.

## Scope

- Update Codex brain skill.
- Update Claude/Hermes standing skills/includes.
- Update mcp2cli Open Brain skill generation.
- Update Open Brain docs and examples.
- Update Hermes memory/provider docs.
- Update any repo-local `AGENTS.md` / `_AGENTS.md` guidance that says `collab` for OB shared memory.
- Use explicit vocabulary:
  - `lane` = channel/thread/task memory
  - `shared-kb` = shared Open Brain knowledge
  - `fs collab` = filesystem/mount/artifacts

## Required Behavior Guidance

- Ongoing channel/thread/task memory stays in the current lane.
- Stable reusable shared knowledge goes to `shared-kb` through explicit promotion or privileged path.
- Repo/project facts go to repo/project fact/entity destination with source pointers.
- Files/artifacts go to fs collab paths, not raw OB blobs.
- `collab` is legacy/internal OB backing only and not client-facing.
- `/mnt/collab` remains filesystem-only and should be called `fs collab`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated mcp2cli Open Brain skill examples use `shared-kb`.
- Codex and Claude skills use `shared-kb`.
- Hermes/Bilby/Skippy guidance uses `shared-kb`.
- No client-facing docs instruct users/agents to write OB memory to `collab`.
- Verification checks can scan for invalid client-facing `collab` wording.
- Host identity is metadata, not namespace identity.
- Rico across AI runtimes uses `rico`; Kevin as person uses `kevin`; Bilby/Skippy as agents use agent identities.

## Non-Goals

- No secrets or token rollout.
- No physical data migration.
- No promoter implementation.

## Traps To Avoid

- Do not equate machine/host with identity.
- Do not make users say `OB` versus `fs` every time; routing should infer the right layer.
- Do not call Kevin an agent unless there is a separate `kevin-agent` process.
